translations.literal: At the end of the Chang'an era, Changzong had already been interrogated by the legal office. Vice Minister of Justice Huan Yanfan judged that his office should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chang'an era, Changzong had already been interrogated by the legal office. Vice Minister of Justice Huan Yanfan judged that his office should be removed.

sentences.zh: 昌宗俄又抗表稱冤，則天意將申理昌宗，廷問宰臣曰：「昌宗於國有功否？」

translations.literal: Soon Changzong again submitted a defiant memorial claiming injustice. Empress Wu intended to vindicate Changzong and asked the chief ministers in court, "Has Changzong rendered service to the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Changzong again submitted a defiant memorial claiming injustice. Empress Wu intended to vindicate Changzong and asked the chief ministers in court, "Has Changzong rendered service to the state?"

sentences.zh: 再思對曰：「昌宗往因合練神丹，聖躬服之有效，此實莫大之功。」

translations.literal: Zaisi replied, "Changzong formerly because he refined the divine elixir, and the sacred person took it with effect — this is truly a service of the greatest magnitude."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi replied, "Changzong formerly because he refined the divine elixir, and the sacred person took it with effect — this is truly a service of the greatest magnitude."

sentences.zh: 則天甚悅，昌宗竟以復職。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly pleased, and Changzong ultimately recovered his office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was greatly pleased, and Changzong ultimately recovered his office.

sentences.zh: 時人貴彥範而賤再思也。

translations.literal: People at the time esteemed Yanfan and despised Zaisi.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time esteemed Yanfan and despised Zaisi.

sentences.zh: 時左補闕戴令言作《兩腳野狐賦》以譏刺之，再思聞之甚怒，出令言爲長社令，朝士尤加嗤笑。

translations.literal: At that time Left Remonstrating Censor Dai Lingyan composed the Rhapsody on the Two-Legged Wild Fox to satirize him. When Zaisi heard of it he was greatly angry and sent Lingyan out as Magistrate of Changshe. Court gentlemen added even more ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Remonstrating Censor Dai Lingyan composed the Rhapsody on the Two-Legged Wild Fox to satirize him. When Zaisi heard of it he was greatly angry and sent Lingyan out as Magistrate of Changshe. Court gentlemen added even more ridicule.

sentences.zh: 再思爲御史大夫時，張易之兄司禮少卿同休嘗奏請公卿大臣宴於司禮寺，預其會者皆盡醉極歡。

translations.literal: When Zaisi was Imperial Censor, Zhang Yizhi's elder brother Tongxiu, Vice Minister of Rites, once memorialized requesting that dukes and ministers feast at the Court of Imperial Rites. Those who attended the gathering all became thoroughly drunk and utterly merry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaisi was Imperial Censor, Zhang Yizhi's elder brother Tongxiu, Vice Minister of Rites, once memorialized requesting that dukes and ministers feast at the Court of Imperial Rites. Those who attended the gathering all became thoroughly drunk and utterly merry.

sentences.zh: 同休戲曰：「楊內史面似高麗。」

translations.literal: Tongxiu joked, "Vice Minister Yang's face resembles that of a Goguryeo."
translations.idiomatic: Tongxiu joked, "Vice Minister Yang's face resembles that of a Goguryeo."

sentences.zh: 再思欣然，請剪紙自貼於巾，卻披紫袍，爲高麗舞，縈頭舒手，舉動合節，滿座嗤笑。

translations.literal: Zaisi was pleased, asked for paper to cut and pasted it on his headcloth, then threw back his purple robe and performed a Goguryeo dance, winding his head and extending his hands, every movement in time. The whole assembly laughed in scorn.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi was pleased, asked for paper to cut and pasted it on his headcloth, then threw back his purple robe and performed a Goguryeo dance, winding his head and extending his hands, every movement in time. The whole assembly laughed in scorn.

sentences.zh: 又易之弟昌宗以姿貌見寵幸，再思又諛之曰：「人言六郎面似蓮花；

translations.literal: Also, Yizhi's younger brother Changzong was favored for his appearance. Zaisi again flattered him, saying, "People say the Sixth Lord's face resembles a lotus;
translations.idiomatic: Also, Yizhi's younger brother Changzong was favored for his appearance. Zaisi again flattered him, saying, "People say the Sixth Lord's face resembles a lotus;

sentences.zh: 再思以爲蓮花似六郎，非六郎似蓮花也。」

translations.literal: Zaisi thinks the lotus resembles the Sixth Lord — not that the Sixth Lord resembles a lotus."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi thinks the lotus resembles the Sixth Lord — not that the Sixth Lord resembles a lotus."

sentences.zh: 其傾巧取媚也如此。

translations.literal: Such was his artful bending to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his artful bending to win favor.

sentences.zh: 長安四年，以本官檢校京兆府長史，又遷檢校揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Chang'an era, in his existing office he was made Acting Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Jingzhao, then transferred to Acting Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chang'an era, in his existing office he was made Acting Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Jingzhao, then transferred to Acting Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，拜戸部尚書，兼中書令，轉侍中，以宮僚封鄭國公，賜實封三百戸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Secretariat Director, then transferred to Palace Attendant. As a palace aide he was enfeoffed Duke of Zheng State and granted three hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Secretariat Director, then transferred to Palace Attendant. As a palace aide he was enfeoffed Duke of Zheng State and granted three hundred households of actual fief.

sentences.zh: 又爲冊順天皇后使，賜物五百段，鞍馬稱是。

translations.literal: He also served as envoy for enfeoffing the Empress of Shuntian and was granted five hundred lengths of goods and saddled horses in fitting measure.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as envoy for enfeoffing the Empress of Shuntian and was granted five hundred lengths of goods and saddled horses in fitting measure.

sentences.zh: 時武三思將誣殺王同皎，再思與吏部尚書李嶠、刑部尚書韋巨源並受製考按其獄，竟不能發明其枉，致同皎至死，眾冤之。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sansi intended to falsely accuse and kill Wang Tongjiao. Zaisi, together with Minister of Personnel Li Jiao and Minister of Punishments Wei Juyuan, all received edicts to examine and try the case. In the end they could not clarify his wrongful treatment and caused Tongjiao to die. All regarded it as a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sansi intended to falsely accuse and kill Wang Tongjiao. Zaisi, together with Minister of Personnel Li Jiao and Minister of Punishments Wei Juyuan, all received edicts to examine and try the case. In the end they could not clarify his wrongful treatment and caused Tongjiao to die. All regarded it as a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 再思俄復爲中書令、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zaisi again became Secretariat Director and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zaisi again became Secretariat Director and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，遷尚書右僕射，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Jinglong era, he was promoted to Right Minister of Works and granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jinglong era, he was promoted to Right Minister of Works and granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 其年薨，贈特進、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: That year he died. He was posthumously appointed Special Advanced and Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Bingzhou, permitted burial at Qianling, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died. He was posthumously appointed Special Advanced and Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Bingzhou, permitted burial at Qianling, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子植、植子獻，並爲司勳員外郎。

translations.literal: His sons Zhi and Zhi's son Xian both served as Vice Directors in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhi and Zhi's son Xian both served as Vice Directors in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 再思弟季昭爲考功郎中，溫玉爲戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: Zaisi's younger brother Jizhao was Director in the Ministry of Personnel; Wenyu was Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi's younger brother Jizhao was Director in the Ministry of Personnel; Wenyu was Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 李懷遠，邢州柏仁人也。

translations.literal: Li Huaiyuan was a native of Bairen in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiyuan was a native of Bairen in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 早孤貧好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, poor, and fond of learning, he was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, poor, and fond of learning, he was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 有宗人欲以高蔭相假者，懷遠竟拒之，退而歎曰：「因人之勢，高士不爲；

translations.literal: A clansman wished to lend him high hereditary privilege for office. Huaiyuan ultimately refused and withdrew, sighing, "To rely on another's power — a lofty man will not do it;
translations.idiomatic: A clansman wished to lend him high hereditary privilege for office. Huaiyuan ultimately refused and withdrew, sighing, "To rely on another's power — a lofty man will not do it;

sentences.zh: 假蔭求官，豈吾本誌？」

translations.literal: to borrow privilege and seek office — is that my original intent?"
translations.idiomatic: to borrow privilege and seek office — is that my original intent?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，應四科舉擢第，累除司禮少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he passed the four categories of examination with highest marks and was appointed in succession Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he passed the four categories of examination with highest marks and was appointed in succession Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出爲邢州刺史，以其本鄉，固辭不就，改授冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Xingzhou. Because it was his home district, he firmly declined and did not accept, and was instead appointed Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Prefect of Xingzhou. Because it was his home district, he firmly declined and did not accept, and was instead appointed Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄暦揚、益等州大都督府長史，未行，又授同州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he served in succession as Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Commands of Yang and Yi, but did not go. He was again appointed Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served in succession as Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Commands of Yang and Yi, but did not go. He was again appointed Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 在職以清簡稱。

translations.literal: In office he was known for purity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was known for purity and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 入爲太子左庶子，兼太子賓客，暦遷右散騎常侍、春官侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince and Concurrent Tutor of the Crown Prince, and was promoted in succession to Right Regular Attendant and Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince and Concurrent Tutor of the Crown Prince, and was promoted in succession to Right Regular Attendant and Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大足年，遷鸞台侍郎，尋同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the Dazu year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Crane Terrace and soon became Concurrent Regulating Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazu year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Crane Terrace and soon became Concurrent Regulating Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，加銀青光祿大夫，拜秋官尚書，兼檢校太子左庶子，賜爵平鄉縣男。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, appointed Minister of the Ministry of Punishments, and made Concurrent Acting Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince. He was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, appointed Minister of the Ministry of Punishments, and made Concurrent Acting Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince. He was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang County.

sentences.zh: 長安四年，以老辭職，聽解秋官尚書，正除太子左庶子，尋授太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Chang'an era, on account of old age he resigned from office. He was permitted to relinquish the Ministry of Punishments and was formally appointed Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince, then soon appointed Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chang'an era, on account of old age he resigned from office. He was permitted to relinquish the Ministry of Punishments and was formally appointed Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince, then soon appointed Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，除左散騎常侍、兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，加金紫光祿大夫，進封趙郡公，特賜實封三百戸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was appointed Left Regular Attendant, Minister of War, and Third-Rank Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal, advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery, and specially granted three hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was appointed Left Regular Attendant, Minister of War, and Third-Rank Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal, advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery, and specially granted three hundred households of actual fief.

sentences.zh: 俄以疾請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of illness he requested retirement and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on account of illness he requested retirement and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 中宗將幸京師，又令以本官知東都留守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong was about to visit the capital, he was again ordered to serve in his existing office as Acting Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was about to visit the capital, he was again ordered to serve in his existing office as Acting Protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 懷遠雖久居榮位，而彌尚簡率，園林宅室，無所改作。

translations.literal: Though Huaiyuan had long held an honored position, he all the more valued simplicity. His gardens and dwelling were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huaiyuan had long held an honored position, he all the more valued simplicity. His gardens and dwelling were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 常乘款段馬，左僕射豆盧欽望謂曰：「公榮貴如此，何不買駿馬乘之？」

translations.literal: He always rode a plain-paced horse. Left Minister of Works Doulu Qinwang said to him, "You are so honored and wealthy — why not buy a fine horse to ride?"
translations.idiomatic: He always rode a plain-paced horse. Left Minister of Works Doulu Qinwang said to him, "You are so honored and wealthy — why not buy a fine horse to ride?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「此馬幸免驚蹶，無假別求。」

translations.literal: He replied, "This horse fortunately escapes stumbling — there is no need to seek another."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "This horse fortunately escapes stumbling — there is no need to seek another."

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不歎美。

translations.literal: Those who heard it all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it all sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年八月卒，中宗特賜錦被以充斂，輟朝一日，親爲文以祭之，贈侍中，諡曰成。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of the Shenlong era he died. Emperor Zhongzong specially granted brocade quilts for his shroud, suspended court audiences for one day, personally composed a text to offer sacrifice, posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of the Shenlong era he died. Emperor Zhongzong specially granted brocade quilts for his shroud, suspended court audiences for one day, personally composed a text to offer sacrifice, posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子景伯。

translations.literal: His son was Jingbo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jingbo.

sentences.zh: 景伯，景龍中爲給事中，又遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Jingbo, during the Jinglong era served as Supervising Secretary and was later promoted to Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo, during the Jinglong era served as Supervising Secretary and was later promoted to Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 中宗嘗宴侍臣及朝集使，酒酣，令各爲《回波辭》。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong once feasted the attending ministers and assembly envoys. When the wine was deep, he ordered each to compose a Huibo lyric.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong once feasted the attending ministers and assembly envoys. When the wine was deep, he ordered each to compose a Huibo lyric.

sentences.zh: 眾皆爲謅佞之辭，及自要榮位。

translations.literal: All composed fawning and flattering words and sought their own glory and position.
translations.idiomatic: All composed fawning and flattering words and sought their own glory and position.

sentences.zh: 次至景伯，曰：「回波爾時酒卮，微臣職在箴規。

translations.literal: When it came to Jingbo, he said, "Huibo, at that time the wine cup — this humble servant's duty lies in admonition and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to Jingbo, he said, "Huibo, at that time the wine cup — this humble servant's duty lies in admonition and regulation.

sentences.zh: 侍宴既過三爵，喧嘩竊恐非儀。」

translations.literal: Attending the feast has already passed three rounds of wine — clamor and noise, I fear, are not proper."
translations.idiomatic: Attending the feast has already passed three rounds of wine — clamor and noise, I fear, are not proper."

sentences.zh: 中宗不悅，中書令蕭至忠稱之曰：「此真諫官也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong was displeased. Secretariat Director Xiao Zhizhong praised him, saying, "This is a true remonstrating official."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong was displeased. Secretariat Director Xiao Zhizhong praised him, saying, "This is a true remonstrating official."

sentences.zh: 景雲中，累遷右散騎常侍，尋以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era he was promoted in succession to Right Regular Attendant and soon retired on account of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era he was promoted in succession to Right Regular Attendant and soon retired on account of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 開元中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 子彭年。

translations.literal: His son was Pengnian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Pengnian.

sentences.zh: 彭年有吏才，工於剖析，當時稱之。

translations.literal: Pengnian had talent for administration and was skilled at analysis. People at the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian had talent for administration and was skilled at analysis. People at the time praised him.

sentences.zh: 開元中，暦考功員外郎、知舉，又遷中書舍人、給事中、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era he served in succession as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Director of Examinations, then was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, Supervising Secretary, and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he served in succession as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Director of Examinations, then was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, Supervising Secretary, and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，又爲吏部侍郎，與右相李林甫善。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he again served as Vice Minister of Personnel and was friendly with Right Chancellor Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he again served as Vice Minister of Personnel and was friendly with Right Chancellor Li Linfu.

sentences.zh: 慕山東著姓爲婚姻，引就清列，以大其門。

translations.literal: He admired taking marriage with eminent surnames east of the mountains and drew them into clear ranks to enlarge his house.
translations.idiomatic: He admired taking marriage with eminent surnames east of the mountains and drew them into clear ranks to enlarge his house.

sentences.zh: 典銓管七年，後以贓汙爲御史中丞宋渾所劾，長流領南臨賀郡。

translations.literal: He managed personnel selection for seven years. Later he was impeached for corruption by Imperial Censor Song Hun and was exiled far to Linhe Commandery in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He managed personnel selection for seven years. Later he was impeached for corruption by Imperial Censor Song Hun and was exiled far to Linhe Commandery in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 累月，渾及第恕又以贓下獄，詔渾流嶺南高要郡，恕流南康郡。

translations.literal: After several months, Hun and his younger brother Shu also went to prison for corruption. An edict exiled Hun to Gaoyao Commandery in Lingnan and Shu to Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After several months, Hun and his younger brother Shu also went to prison for corruption. An edict exiled Hun to Gaoyao Commandery in Lingnan and Shu to Nankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載，起彭年爲濟陰太守，又遷馮翊太守，入爲中書舍人、給事中、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, Pengnian was recalled as Prefect of Jiyin, then transferred to Prefect of Fengyi, and entered the capital as Secretariat Drafter, Supervising Secretary, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, Pengnian was recalled as Prefect of Jiyin, then transferred to Prefect of Fengyi, and entered the capital as Secretariat Drafter, Supervising Secretary, and Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五載，玄宗幸蜀，賊陷西京。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu. The rebels seized the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu. The rebels seized the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 彭年沒於賊，脅授僞官，憂憤忽忽不得志，與韋斌相次而卒。

translations.literal: Pengnian fell into the hands of the rebels, was compelled to accept a false office, and died in grief and dejection without achieving his intent, following Wei Bin in dying one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian fell into the hands of the rebels, was compelled to accept a false office, and died in grief and dejection without achieving his intent, following Wei Bin in dying one after another.

sentences.zh: 及克復兩京，優製贈彭年爲禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, a generous edict posthumously appointed Pengnian Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, a generous edict posthumously appointed Pengnian Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 豆盧欽望，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Doulu Qinwang was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Qinwang was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖通，隋相州刺史、南陳郡公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tong was Military Governor of Xiangzhou and Duke of Nanchen Commandery in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tong was Military Governor of Xiangzhou and Duke of Nanchen Commandery in Sui.

sentences.zh: 祖寬，即隋文帝之甥也。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuan was the nephew of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuan was the nephew of Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 大業末，爲梁泉令。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was Magistrate of Liangquan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he was Magistrate of Liangquan.

sentences.zh: 及高祖定關中，寬與郡守蕭瑀率豪右赴京師，由是累授殿中監，仍詔其子懷讓尚萬春公主。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified Guanzhong, Kuan together with the prefect Xiao Yu led the local magnates to the capital and was therefore appointed in succession Supervisor of the Palace and also ordered that his son Huairang marry Princess Wanchun.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor pacified Guanzhong, Kuan together with the prefect Xiao Yu led the local magnates to the capital and was therefore appointed in succession Supervisor of the Palace and also ordered that his son Huairang marry Princess Wanchun.

sentences.zh: 高祖以寬曾祖萇魏太和中例稱單姓，至是改寬爲盧氏。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, because Kuan's great-grandfather Chang in the Wei Taihe era was by precedent called by a single surname, at this time changed Kuan's surname to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor, because Kuan's great-grandfather Chang in the Wei Taihe era was by precedent called by a single surname, at this time changed Kuan's surname to Lu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，暦遷禮部尚書、左衛大將軍，封芮國公。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era he was promoted in succession to Minister of Rites and Grand General of the Left Guard, and was enfeoffed Duke of Rui State.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was promoted in succession to Minister of Rites and Grand General of the Left Guard, and was enfeoffed Duke of Rui State.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年卒，贈特進、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，諡曰定。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Yonghui era he died, posthumously appointed Special Advanced and Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Bingzhou, permitted burial at Zhaoling, with the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yonghui era he died, posthumously appointed Special Advanced and Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Bingzhou, permitted burial at Zhaoling, with the posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 又復其姓爲豆盧氏。

translations.literal: His surname was also restored to Doulu.
translations.idiomatic: His surname was also restored to Doulu.

sentences.zh: 父仁業，高宗時爲左衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Renye was General of the Left Guard during the reign of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renye was General of the Left Guard during the reign of Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 欽望，則天時累遷司賓卿。

translations.literal: Qinwang, during Empress Wu's time, was promoted in succession to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang, during Empress Wu's time, was promoted in succession to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，代宗秦客爲內史。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Changshou era he replaced Zong Qinke as Inner Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Changshou era he replaced Zong Qinke as Inner Scribe.

sentences.zh: 時李昭德亦爲內史，執權用事，欽望與同時宰相韋巨源、陸元方、蘇味道、杜景儉等並委曲從之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhaode also served as Inner Scribe, wielded power and managed affairs, and Qinwang together with the chief ministers of the time Wei Juyuan, Lu Yuanfang, Su Weidao, and Du Jingjian all bent and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zhaode also served as Inner Scribe, wielded power and managed affairs, and Qinwang together with the chief ministers of the time Wei Juyuan, Lu Yuanfang, Su Weidao, and Du Jingjian all bent and followed him.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，昭德坐事，左遷涪陵尉，則天以欽望等不能執正，又爲司刑少卿皇甫文備奏欽望附會昭德，罔上附下，乃左遷欽望爲趙州刺史，韋巨源自右丞爲鄜州刺史，陸元方自秋官侍郎爲綏州刺史，蘇味道自鳳閣侍郎爲集州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhengsheng era, Zhaode was punished for an offense and demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Fuling. Empress Wu, because Qinwang and the others could not uphold what was right, and because Vice Minister of Justice Huangfu Wenbei also memorialized that Qinwang had attached himself to Zhaode and deceived superiors while attaching to inferiors, demoted Qinwang to Prefect of Zhao, Wei Juyuan from Right Vice Director to Prefect of Fu, Lu Yuanfang from Vice Minister of Punishments to Prefect of Sui, and Su Weidao from Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion to Prefect of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhengsheng era, Zhaode was punished for an offense and demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Fuling. Empress Wu, because Qinwang and the others could not uphold what was right, and because Vice Minister of Justice Huangfu Wenbei also memorialized that Qinwang had attached himself to Zhaode and deceived superiors while attaching to inferiors, demoted Qinwang to Prefect of Zhao, Wei Juyuan from Right Vice Director to Prefect of Fu, Lu Yuanfang from Vice Minister of Punishments to Prefect of Sui, and Su Weidao from Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion to Prefect of Ji.

sentences.zh: 其年，欽望入爲司禮卿，遷秋官尚書，封芮國公。

translations.literal: That year Qinwang entered the capital as Minister of Rites, was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Punishments, and was enfeoffed Duke of Rui State.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qinwang entered the capital as Minister of Rites, was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Punishments, and was enfeoffed Duke of Rui State.

sentences.zh: 出爲河北道宣勞使。

translations.literal: He went out as Commissioner for Proclaiming Comfort on the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Commissioner for Proclaiming Comfort on the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄而廬陵王復爲皇太子，以欽望爲皇太子宮尹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Prince of Luling was again made Crown Prince, and Qinwang was appointed Director of the Crown Prince's Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Prince of Luling was again made Crown Prince, and Qinwang was appointed Director of the Crown Prince's Palace.

sentences.zh: 聖暦二年，拜文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品，尋授太子賓客，停知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Shengli era he was appointed Right Minister of the Department of Literature and Third-Rank Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, then appointed Tutor of the Crown Prince and stopped managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Shengli era he was appointed Right Minister of the Department of Literature and Third-Rank Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, then appointed Tutor of the Crown Prince and stopped managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以欽望宮僚舊臣，拜尚書左僕射、知軍國重事，兼檢校安國相王府長史，兼中書令、知兵部事、監修國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, because Qinwang was an old minister of the palace staff, he was appointed Left Minister of Works, Manager of Important Military Affairs, Concurrent Acting Chief Administrator of the Princely Mansion of Anguo and Xiang, Concurrent Secretariat Director, Manager of the Ministry of War, and Supervisor of Compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, because Qinwang was an old minister of the palace staff, he was appointed Left Minister of Works, Manager of Important Military Affairs, Concurrent Acting Chief Administrator of the Princely Mansion of Anguo and Xiang, Concurrent Secretariat Director, Manager of the Ministry of War, and Supervisor of Compiling the National History.

sentences.zh: 欽望作相兩朝，前後十餘年，張易之兄弟及武三思父子皆專權驕縱，圖爲逆亂。

translations.literal: Qinwang served as chief minister across two reigns for more than ten years in all. The Zhang Yizhi brothers and the father and sons Wu Sansi all monopolized power and were arrogant and unrestrained, plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang served as chief minister across two reigns for more than ten years in all. The Zhang Yizhi brothers and the father and sons Wu Sansi all monopolized power and were arrogant and unrestrained, plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 欽望獨謹其身，不能有所匡正，以此獲譏於代。

translations.literal: Qinwang alone kept himself cautious and could not correct them. For this he received reproach from his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang alone kept himself cautious and could not correct them. For this he received reproach from his generation.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，拜開府儀。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Shenlong era he was appointed Grand Marshal of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Shenlong era he was appointed Grand Marshal of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年五月，表請氣骸，不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of the Jinglong era he submitted a memorial requesting to retire on account of declining health. This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of the Jinglong era he submitted a memorial requesting to retire on account of declining health. This was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 十一月卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died, at more than eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he died, at more than eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、并州大都督，諡曰元，賜東園秘器，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Yuan, granted the Eastern Garden funerary vessels, and permitted burial at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and Chief Administrator of the Superior Area Command of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Yuan, granted the Eastern Garden funerary vessels, and permitted burial at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 則天時，宰相又有張光輔、史務滋、崔元綜、周允元等，並有名績。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time there were also chief ministers Zhang Guangfu, Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, Zhou Yun'yuan, and others, all of whom had fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's time there were also chief ministers Zhang Guangfu, Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, Zhou Yun'yuan, and others, all of whom had fame and achievement.

sentences.zh: 張光輔者，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangfu was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangfu was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少明辯，有吏幹。

translations.literal: From youth he was clear in debate and had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clear in debate and had administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 累遷司農少卿、文昌右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Revenue and Right Vice Minister of the Department of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Revenue and Right Vice Minister of the Department of Literature.

sentences.zh: 以討平越王貞之功，拜鳳閣侍郎、知政事。

translations.literal: For the achievement of suppressing Prince Zhen of Yue, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Manager of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For the achievement of suppressing Prince Zhen of Yue, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Manager of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，遷納言。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Yongchang era he was promoted to Chief Minister of Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongchang era he was promoted to Chief Minister of Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 旬日，又拜內史。

translations.literal: Ten days later he was again appointed Inner Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he was again appointed Inner Scribe.

sentences.zh: 皆有名。

translations.literal: All were famous posts.
translations.idiomatic: All were famous posts.

sentences.zh: 其年，洛州司馬房嗣業、洛陽令張嗣明坐與徐敬業弟敬真陰相交結。

translations.literal: That year, Vice Military Governor of Luozhou Fang Siye and Magistrate of Luoyang Zhang Siming were punished for secretly associating with Xu Jingye's younger brother Jingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Vice Military Governor of Luozhou Fang Siye and Magistrate of Luoyang Zhang Siming were punished for secretly associating with Xu Jingye's younger brother Jingzhen.

sentences.zh: 敬真自流所繡州逃歸，將北投突厥，引虜入寇。

translations.literal: Jingzhen escaped from exile in Xiuzhou and returned, intending to go north and join the Turks and lead the barbarians in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen escaped from exile in Xiuzhou and returned, intending to go north and join the Turks and lead the barbarians in invasion.

sentences.zh: 途經洛下，嗣業、嗣明二人給其衣糧而遣之。

translations.literal: Passing through Luoyang, Siye and Siming supplied him with clothing and grain and sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Luoyang, Siye and Siming supplied him with clothing and grain and sent him on.

sentences.zh: 行至定州，爲人所覺。

translations.literal: When he reached Dingzhou he was discovered by others.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Dingzhou he was discovered by others.

sentences.zh: 嗣業於獄中自縊死。

translations.literal: Siye hanged himself in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Siye hanged himself in prison.

sentences.zh: 嗣明與敬真多引海內相識，冀緩其死。

translations.literal: Siming and Jingzhen implicated many acquaintances throughout the realm, hoping to delay their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Siming and Jingzhen implicated many acquaintances throughout the realm, hoping to delay their deaths.

sentences.zh: 嗣明稱光輔征豫州日，私說圖識天文，陰懷兩端，顧望以觀成敗。

translations.literal: Siming said that when Guangfu campaigned at Yuzhou, he privately discussed prognostications and astronomy and secretly harbored two minds, looking about to observe success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Siming said that when Guangfu campaigned at Yuzhou, he privately discussed prognostications and astronomy and secretly harbored two minds, looking about to observe success or failure.

sentences.zh: 光輔由是被誅，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: Guangfu was thereby executed, and his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu was thereby executed, and his household was registered and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 史務滋者，宣州溧陽人。

translations.literal: Shi Wuzi was a native of Liyang in Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wuzi was a native of Liyang in Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累至內史。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Inner Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Inner Scribe.

sentences.zh: 天授中，雅州刺史劉行實及弟渠州刺史行瑜、尚衣奉禦行感，並兄子左鷹揚將軍虔通，並爲侍御史來子珣誣以謀反誅。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era, Regional Inspector of Yazhou Liu Xingshi and his younger brother Regional Inspector of Quzhou Liu Xingyu, Palace Attendant for Imperial Vestments Liu Xinggan, and his elder brother's son Left General of the Hawkish Guard Liu Qiantong were all falsely accused of plotting rebellion by Attending Censor Lai Zixun and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era, Regional Inspector of Yazhou Liu Xingshi and his younger brother Regional Inspector of Quzhou Liu Xingyu, Palace Attendant for Imperial Vestments Liu Xinggan, and his elder brother's son Left General of the Hawkish Guard Liu Qiantong were all falsely accused of plotting rebellion by Attending Censor Lai Zixun and were executed.

sentences.zh: 又於盱眙毀其父左監門大將軍伯英棺柩。

translations.literal: Also at Xuyi they destroyed the coffin of their father, Grand General of the Left Gate Guards Bo Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Also at Xuyi they destroyed the coffin of their father, Grand General of the Left Gate Guards Bo Ying.

sentences.zh: 初，務滋素與行感周密，意俗寢其反狀。

translations.literal: At first Wuzi had long been on intimate terms with Xinggan and expected that the charges of rebellion could be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wuzi had long been on intimate terms with Xinggan and expected that the charges of rebellion could be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 則天怒，令俊臣鞫之，務滋恐被陷刑，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was angry and ordered Junchen to interrogate him. Wuzi, fearing he would be trapped in punishment, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was angry and ordered Junchen to interrogate him. Wuzi, fearing he would be trapped in punishment, then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 崔元綜者，鄭州新鄭人也。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanzong was a native of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanzong was a native of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖君肅，武德中黃門侍郎、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junsu was Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Minister of Diplomacy during the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Junsu was Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Minister of Diplomacy during the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 元綜，天授中累轉秋官侍郎。

translations.literal: Yuanzong, during the Tianshou era, was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzong, during the Tianshou era, was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 長壽元年，遷鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Changshou era he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Crane Terrace and Concurrent Regulating Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Changshou era he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Crane Terrace and Concurrent Regulating Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 元綜勤於政事，每在中書，必束帶至晚，未嘗休偃。

translations.literal: Yuanzong was diligent in government affairs. Whenever he was in the Secretariat he always wore his belt until evening and never rested reclining.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzong was diligent in government affairs. Whenever he was in the Secretariat he always wore his belt until evening and never rested reclining.

sentences.zh: 好潔細行，薰辛不暦口者二十餘年。

translations.literal: He loved purity in small conduct and for more than twenty years did not let pungent or acrid flavors pass his lips.
translations.idiomatic: He loved purity in small conduct and for more than twenty years did not let pungent or acrid flavors pass his lips.

sentences.zh: 雖外示謹厚，而情深刻薄，每受製鞫獄，必披毛求疵，陷於重辟。

translations.literal: Though outwardly he showed cautious generosity, inwardly his feelings were harsh and mean. Whenever he received edicts to interrogate cases, he always split hairs seeking flaws and trapped people in heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though outwardly he showed cautious generosity, inwardly his feelings were harsh and mean. Whenever he received edicts to interrogate cases, he always split hairs seeking flaws and trapped people in heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 以此故人多畏而鄙之。

translations.literal: For this reason many feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 明年，犯罪配流振州，朝野莫不稱慶。

translations.literal: The next year, for a crime he was sentenced to exile in Zhenzhou. Court and common people alike all called it a celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, for a crime he was sentenced to exile in Zhenzhou. Court and common people alike all called it a celebration.

sentences.zh: 尋赦還，復拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned and returned, and was again appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was pardoned and returned, and was again appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，累遷尚書左丞、蒲州刺史，以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Zhongzong he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Pu and retired on account of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhongzong he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Pu and retired on account of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 晚年好攝養導引之術，年九十餘卒。

translations.literal: In his later years he loved nourishing and guiding practices and died at more than ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he loved nourishing and guiding practices and died at more than ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 周允元者，豫州人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Yun'yuan was a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yun'yuan was a native of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 延戴初，累轉左肅政御史中丞，俄除鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanzai era he was promoted in succession to Left Imperial Censor and soon appointed Concurrent Regulating Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanzai era he was promoted in succession to Left Imperial Censor and soon appointed Concurrent Regulating Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 嘗與諸宰臣侍宴，則天令各述書傳中善言。

translations.literal: He once attended a feast with the chief ministers. Empress Wu ordered each to recite a good saying from books and records.
translations.idiomatic: He once attended a feast with the chief ministers. Empress Wu ordered each to recite a good saying from books and records.

sentences.zh: 允元曰：「恥其君不如堯、舜。」

translations.literal: Yun'yuan said, "To be ashamed that one's lord is not like Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan said, "To be ashamed that one's lord is not like Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 武三思以爲語有指斥，糾而駁之。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi held that the words contained pointed criticism and impeached and refuted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi held that the words contained pointed criticism and impeached and refuted him.

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「聞此言足以爲誡，豈特將爲過耶？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu said, "Hearing these words is enough to serve as a warning — how could it be taken only as an offense?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said, "Hearing these words is enough to serve as a warning — how could it be taken only as an offense?"

sentences.zh: 證聖元年卒，贈貝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhengsheng era he died and was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhengsheng era he died and was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 則天爲七言詩以傷之，又自繕寫，時以爲榮。

translations.literal: Empress Wu composed a seven-character poem to mourn him and copied it out herself. People at the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu composed a seven-character poem to mourn him and copied it out herself. People at the time regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 史官曰：王及善在孝敬東宮，誠能奉職。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the Eastern Palace of Respectful Filiality, Wang Jishan truly was able to perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: In the Eastern Palace of Respectful Filiality, Wang Jishan truly was able to perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 當俊臣下獄，力諫除凶，是憂濫及賢良，而欲明彰羽翼，興復之誌，不謂無心。

translations.literal: When Junchen was imprisoned, he forcefully remonstrated to eliminate the villain — this was concern that harm would spread to the worthy, and the wish to make clear the support of wings. The intent of restoration was not without heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Junchen was imprisoned, he forcefully remonstrated to eliminate the villain — this was concern that harm would spread to the worthy, and the wish to make clear the support of wings. The intent of restoration was not without heart.

sentences.zh: 杜景儉五刑有濫，濟活爲心，四氣不和，歸罪在己，則天謂曰「真宰相。」

translations.literal: Du Jingjian, when the five punishments were abused, took saving lives as his heart; when the four seasons were out of harmony, he attributed the fault to himself. Empress Wu called him a "true chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingjian, when the five punishments were abused, took saving lives as his heart; when the four seasons were out of harmony, he attributed the fault to himself. Empress Wu called him a "true chief minister."

sentences.zh: 然奈柔順李昭德，不無吐剛之過也。

translations.literal: Yet in yielding to the compliant Li Zhaode, he was not without the fault of spitting out what was hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in yielding to the compliant Li Zhaode, he was not without the fault of spitting out what was hard.

sentences.zh: 朱敬則文學有稱，節行無愧，諫諍果決，推擇精真，苟非洞鑒古今，深識王霸，何由立其高論哉？

translations.literal: Zhu Jingze was famed for literature, his conduct was without shame, his remonstrance was decisive, and his selection of men was precise and true. Had he not thoroughly discerned past and present and deeply understood kingship and hegemony, how could he have established such lofty discourse?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jingze was famed for literature, his conduct was without shame, his remonstrance was decisive, and his selection of men was precise and true. Had he not thoroughly discerned past and present and deeply understood kingship and hegemony, how could he have established such lofty discourse?

sentences.zh: 惜乎相不得時矣。

translations.literal: Alas, as chief minister he did not meet the right time.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, as chief minister he did not meet the right time.

sentences.zh: 楊再思佞而取貴，苟以全身，掩不善而自欺，謂無十目十手也。

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi was fawning and thereby gained honor, preserving himself as he could, covering what was not good and deceiving himself — as though there were not ten eyes and ten hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi was fawning and thereby gained honor, preserving himself as he could, covering what was not good and deceiving himself — as though there were not ten eyes and ten hands.

sentences.zh: 李懷遠名不苟於假蔭，貴不衒於故鄉，無改陋居，常乘劣駟，亦一時之善矣。

translations.literal: Li Huaiyuan's fame was not tainted by borrowed privilege; his honor did not flaunt his home district; he did not alter his humble dwelling and always rode a poor horse — this too was a goodness of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiyuan's fame was not tainted by borrowed privilege; his honor did not flaunt his home district; he did not alter his humble dwelling and always rode a poor horse — this too was a goodness of the time.

sentences.zh: 然匪躬之道，未之聞也。

translations.literal: Yet the way of not sparing oneself — of this one has not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the way of not sparing oneself — of this one has not heard.

sentences.zh: 豆盧欽望、張光輔、史務滋、崔元綜、周允元等，或有片言，非無小善，登於大用，可謂具臣。

translations.literal: Doulu Qinwang, Zhang Guangfu, Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, Zhou Yun'yuan, and the like — some had a phrase, and none were without small goodness. Raised to great employment, they may be called complete ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Qinwang, Zhang Guangfu, Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, Zhou Yun'yuan, and the like — some had a phrase, and none were without small goodness. Raised to great employment, they may be called complete ministers.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：及善奉職，非無智力。

translations.literal: Praise says: Jishan performed his duties — he was not without intelligence and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Praise says: Jishan performed his duties — he was not without intelligence and strength.

sentences.zh: 景儉當權，不謂不賢。

translations.literal: Jingjian held power — he cannot be called unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian held power — he cannot be called unworthy.

sentences.zh: 雄文高節，少連爲絶。

translations.literal: Mighty writing and lofty integrity — Shaolian stands supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Mighty writing and lofty integrity — Shaolian stands supreme.

sentences.zh: 守道安貧，懷遠當仁。

translations.literal: Keeping the way and content with poverty — Huaiyuan met the standard of benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping the way and content with poverty — Huaiyuan met the standard of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 欽望之屬，片善何足。

translations.literal: The sort of Qinwang — what small goodness is enough?
translations.idiomatic: The sort of Qinwang — what small goodness is enough?

sentences.zh: 諂媚再思，隻宜遄速。

translations.literal: To fawn on Zaisi — one ought only to hurry away.
translations.idiomatic: To fawn on Zaisi — one ought only to hurry away.
